source: Hand-entered from the alignment-events research (bq2vila6z.txt §C1–C7) and the plan's "events (geometric)" and "events (almanac sanity)" verification rows; every row carries its source URL and basis. Horizons values are the research's own API runs (not published almanac numbers).

conventions.times: UTC, 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM[:SS]'. Espenak hour-only values are stored as hh:30 (the ±30 min half-hour convention, final critique byf0bzyiw.txt). in-the-sky.org values carry hh:mm only, with the calendar date taken from Horizons/Espenak because that site shows some dates one day early (research §0 'ITS').
conventions.basis: 'geometric-horizons' = JPL Horizons VECTORS with VEC_CORR=NONE (no light-time, no aberration, J2000 ecliptic), the same model class as this app's VSOP87 pipeline; 'apparent-almanac' = published apparent geocentric phenomena, which differ from geometric instants by 6–40 min (oppositions/conjunctions) and by up to a few hours (greatest elongations) — research §A 'Geometric vs apparent'.
conventions.bodies: ids in Sun-outward order (events.js sorts bodies the same way)
conventions.tolerances: per row: tolMin (minutes, on utc), tolMinLambda (minutes, on lambdaUtc), tolDays (on date), expect.tolDeg / tolArcmin / tolArcsec / tolAu / tolKm on the named value; rows with `excluded` are recorded but not asserted
conventions.hourOnly: Espenak page: "Inferior/Superior Conjunctions (Mercury & Venus) ± 30 minutes; Greatest Elongation ± 30 minutes; Aphelion/Perihelion ± 30 minutes; Earth perihelion ±0.00001 AU"

sources.HZG: https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api — JPL Horizons API, EPHEM_TYPE=VECTORS, VEC_CORR=NONE, REF_PLANE=ECLIPTIC, REF_SYSTEM=ICRF, TIME_TYPE=UT (geometric, no light-time/aberration; research bq2vila6z.txt §0 "HZG", 5-min/2-min grid, ±1–2 min)
sources.HZA: https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/api/horizons.api — JPL Horizons API, EPHEM_TYPE=OBSERVER, CENTER=500@399, QUANTITIES 2,20,23,31 (apparent; research §0 "HZA")
sources.ITS: https://in-the-sky.org/news.php?id=YYYYMMDD_NN_10x (NN: 11 inner-planet, 12 outer-planet, 15 appulse, 20 conjunction = same RA); e.g. https://in-the-sky.org/news.php?id=20240908_12_100

geometric.note: JPL Horizons API, EPHEM_TYPE=VECTORS, VEC_CORR=NONE, REF_PLANE=ECLIPTIC, REF_SYSTEM=ICRF, TIME_TYPE=UT (geometric, no light-time/aberration; research bq2vila6z.txt §0 "HZG", 5-min/2-min grid, ±1–2 min); research §C1

extremum.note: Maximum of the APPARENT S-O-T elongation (research §C1 "max ψ 175.7125° at 01:42", HZA column). The maximum is flat (curvature 1.1e-7 °/min²): the geometric vertex measured with VSOP87 lies at 01:54 (ψ differs by 1.8e-5° between the two instants), so the plan's ±10 min is widened to ±20 min = 1.5 × the measured 12.5 min offset.

geometric.note: Transit of Venus 2012: HZA apparent λ inferior conjunction 01:08 UT; geometric ≈ 6 min earlier (final critique byf0bzyiw.txt, Venus IC offset measured for 2025). NASA/Espenak geocentric minimum separation 554″ at greatest transit 01:29:36 UT.

extremum.note: "minimum separation from the Sun is 554 arc-seconds" (geocentric)

geometric.note: Great conjunction 2020: HZG geometric minimum 18:11 / λ-conjunction 18:10 (research §C4, §C5); Wikipedia: closest separation 18:20 UTC, 6.1′ (apparent)
